title: LLM Cache Pricing 2026: The Real Cost of Cached Input
description: LLM cache pricing 2026 normalized across six providers: effective input cost at real hit rates, hidden write fees, and which vendors publish nothing at all.

attribution.citation: Json House, "LLM Cache Pricing 2026: The Real Cost of Cached Input", jsonhouse.com (2026-08-03)

key_facts.fact: The cached-read discount converged on exactly 90% of base input at Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google; xAI discounts 84-85% and DeepSeek 98-99.2%
key_facts.source: jsonhouse normalization of six official pricing pages, 2026-07-28

key_facts.fact: Effective input price is base x (1 - h) + cache_read x h, where h is the share of input tokens served from cache
The cheapest model by effective input cost changes at an 84.7% cache hit rate: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite below it, DeepSeek v4-flash above it, both costing $0.0237 per 1M at the crossover
OpenAI introduced a 1.25x cache-write charge with the GPT-5.6 family; models before it had no write fee

Anthropic charges 1.25x base input for a 5-minute cache write and 2x for a 1-hour write, has no storage fee, and sets a minimum cacheable prompt length of 512 tokens on Opus 5 and Fable 5 rising to 4,096 on Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, and Haiku 4.5 — below which requests are processed uncached and without an error
key_facts.source: Anthropic pricing page and prompt caching documentation, retrieved 2026-07-28

key_facts.fact: Google charges no cache write fee but bills storage at $1.00 per 1M cached tokens per hour, rising to $4.50 on Gemini 2.5 Pro and 3.1 Pro Preview
Four of the six providers publish no cache TTL, and Mistral publishes no per-model cache price at all, stating only a headline -90% for cached input
key_facts.source: jsonhouse normalization of six official documentation sets, 2026-07-28

key_facts.fact: A 50,000-token prompt sent on 1,000 Claude Sonnet 5 calls costs $100.00 uncached and $10.12 with the 5-minute cache including its 1.25x write, an 89.9% saving

OpenAI's documentation does not state whether a cache write is billed on a prompt that is never reused; it says an eligible prefix 'may' be cached, and offers prompt_cache_options.mode set to explicit as an opt-out

faq_summary.q: How much does prompt caching actually save in 2026?
faq_summary.a: The discount is 90% at Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, 84-85% at xAI, and 98-99% at DeepSeek. It applies only to the cached share of a prompt, so the realized saving is roughly hit rate times discount — a 50% hit rate against a 90% discount is a 45% cut.

faq_summary.q: Do you pay to write to the cache?
faq_summary.a: Anthropic always charges: 1.25x base input for a 5-minute write, 2x for an hour. OpenAI added the same 1.25x charge with GPT-5.6 and charged nothing before it. Google charges storage per hour instead. xAI, DeepSeek, and Mistral publish no write price.

faq_summary.q: Which LLM API is cheapest for a cache-heavy agent?
faq_summary.a: It depends on hit rate. Below roughly 83% Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is cheapest per effective input token; above it DeepSeek v4-flash leads, reaching $0.0097 per 1M at a 95% hit rate.

faq_summary.q: Is prompt caching automatic or do I have to enable it?
faq_summary.a: OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and xAI cache automatically; Anthropic requires an explicit cache_control field. Because GPT-5.6 caches automatically above 1,024 tokens and bills writes at 1.25x, a prompt you never reuse may bill above base rate unless you opt out.

faq_summary.q: Why can't I compare cache prices straight from provider pricing pages?
faq_summary.a: No two publish the same fields. Anthropic gives multipliers, DeepSeek an absolute cache-hit price, xAI one cached-input column, Google a per-hour storage rate, and Mistral only a headline -90%. Four of six publish no TTL.
